All work is complete and verified. The remaining `"main"` references are correctly out of scope: line 795 is my intentional fallback (reproducing today's behaviour), the `git fetch origin main` calls already target origin, and the `--base main` / `_sync_branch` defaults are GitHub PR base **branch names** (which must be bare names, not remote-tracking refs).

## Result
- Goal/task: G-20260805T023333273780Z-cd2e69ec / T-20260805T023333275527Z-fff69d84
- Role: Implementer (Claude Code)
- Status: ready — implementation complete, all acceptance gates green. The Shiki loop owns commit/push/PR/merge.

## What changed
- **`scripts/shiki_loop.py`** — added a shared `_default_base_ref(target)` helper that calls `shiki_runtime.resolve_default_branch_ref` (imported into the existing line-30 import, not reimplemented) and degrades to bare `"main"` on any failure so it never raises into the loop. Wired it into all three sites:
  - ahead-count: `git rev-list --count {base}..HEAD` (was `main..HEAD`)
  - reviewer diff: `git diff --cached {base}` (was `--cached main`)
  - fallback: `git diff {base}...HEAD` (was `main...HEAD`)
  - Corrected the reviewer-diff comment and the `_CODE_REVIEW_PROMPT` string that named a bare `main`.
- **`tests/test_loop_code_review.py`** — new `ReviewerDiffBaseTests` builds a real repo whose local `main` (and tracking ref) lag a 60-file merged remote history, cuts the task branch from the true remote tip, drives `_run_pre_pr_code_review` with a stdin-capturing reviewer stub, and asserts the captured diff is **exactly 1 file** (`feature.py`), excludes `bulk/`, and is `< stale_diff/10` bytes.
- **`tests/test_repair_delivery.py`** — `worktree_commits_beyond_main` now resolves its base via `resolve_default_branch_ref` (same call the loop makes) so harness and loop can't drift; `RepairEnv` pins `origin/HEAD → origin/main` for deterministic resolution.
